investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T15:34:53–56Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm-level error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every downstream check, the quota rejection prevented any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected, causing all three checks to fail with zero evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the eval org has reached or exceeded the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because the runner calls createAgent() as the first operation in the remote-agent-create probe (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339), the 409 is returned before any evidence can be written, causing all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and all three remote-agents checks to fail with the same message. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a resource-quota condition in the production swarm API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm API rejected the creation request before any agent was provisioned.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting at the createAgent() call before any evidence could be written.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both sibling checks carry the identical 409 message and zero evidence keys, confirming the failure originates at the shared createAgent() call rather than in check-specific logic.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1331-1339: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after resolving orgId; a 409 at this point terminates the withCleanup block before any evidence is recorded.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1272 — the call returned in ~1.3 s, consistent with a fast quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or VM provisioning failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:147-155: remote-agent-create is marked required=true and degradedAfterFailures=1, so this single failure is sufficient to mark the remote-agents feature degraded in the observability dashboard.
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm agent quota exhausted for the eval org: the production swarm API enforces a hard limit of 100 agents per org; the eval org has reached that limit, possibly due to leaked agents from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up by the withCleanup() mechanism.

Secondary — Cleanup failure from a previous eval run: if a prior run's withCleanup() block failed to delete a remote agent (e.g., due to a crash or network error), agents accumulate over time and eventually exhaust the quota.

Tertiary — Eval org misconfiguration: the eval credentials may be scoped to an org that is shared with non-eval workloads, causing the quota to be consumed by production agents rather than eval artifacts.

Lower probability — Swarm service quota enforcement bug: the swarm service may be incorrectly counting agents or applying a stricter limit than intended, but the explicit 'limit is 100' message makes a misconfiguration on the eval-org side more likely.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2015) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner is unreachable or misconfigured. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=142234, generation_completed frame and imageUrlPresent=true observed), isolating the failure strictly to the production-api harness target and not to the image generation feature itself.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api agent runtime harness endpoint is returning HTTP 404 when the eval runner calls /api/generate/image/stream. The stream emits a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and the message "agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version." This prevents the session from opening, so no generation_completed frame is ever emitted and no image URL is produced, causing both contract assertions to fail. The failure is localized to the production-api runtime environment; the desktop-release variant of the same check passed in the same run window. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so this is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api harness target, not a confirmed user-facing outage. The most likely cause is a misconfigured or absent SWARM_BASE_URL / LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable pointing to a non-existent or incompatible harness deployment for the production-api runtime.

failed-check.message: check message explicitly states '404' and instructs to 'Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2015 — the check failed in ~2 seconds, consistent with an immediate 404 response rather than a generation timeout (warningLatencyMs=180000, outageLatencyMs=360000).

sibling.image-generation-stream: the desktop-release variant of the same check passed (status=pass, latencyMs=142234) with generation_completed present and imageUrlPresent=true, proving the image generation feature itself is functional and the failure is environment-specific.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T15:34:53–56Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm-level error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every downstream check, the quota rejection prevented any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected, causing all three checks to fail with zero evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the eval org has reached or exceeded the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because the runner calls createAgent() as the first operation in the remote-agent-create probe (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339), the 409 is returned before any evidence can be written, causing all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and all three remote-agents checks to fail with the same message. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a resource-quota condition in the production swarm API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm API rejected the creation request before any agent was provisioned.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting at the createAgent() call before any evidence could be written.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both sibling checks carry the identical 409 message and zero evidence keys, confirming the failure originates at the shared createAgent() call rather than in check-specific logic.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1331-1339: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after resolving orgId; a 409 at this point terminates the withCleanup block before any evidence is recorded.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1272 — the call returned in ~1.3 s, consistent with a fast quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or VM provisioning failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:147-155: remote-agent-create is marked required=true and degradedAfterFailures=1, so this single failure is sufficient to mark the remote-agents feature degraded in the observability dashboard.
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm agent quota exhausted for the eval org: the production swarm API enforces a hard limit of 100 agents per org; the eval org has reached that limit, possibly due to leaked agents from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up by the withCleanup() mechanism.

Secondary — Cleanup failure from a previous eval run: if a prior run's withCleanup() block failed to delete a remote agent (e.g., due to a crash or network error), agents accumulate over time and eventually exhaust the quota.

Tertiary — Eval org misconfiguration: the eval credentials may be scoped to an org that is shared with non-eval workloads, causing the quota to be consumed by production agents rather than eval artifacts.

Lower probability — Swarm service quota enforcement bug: the swarm service may be incorrectly counting agents or applying a stricter limit than intended, but the explicit 'limit is 100' message makes a misconfiguration on the eval-org side more likely.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2015) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner is unreachable or misconfigured. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=142234, generation_completed frame and imageUrlPresent=true observed), isolating the failure strictly to the production-api harness target and not to the image generation feature itself.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api agent runtime harness endpoint is returning HTTP 404 when the eval runner calls /api/generate/image/stream. The stream emits a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and the message "agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version." This prevents the session from opening, so no generation_completed frame is ever emitted and no image URL is produced, causing both contract assertions to fail. The failure is localized to the production-api runtime environment; the desktop-release variant of the same check passed in the same run window. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so this is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api harness target, not a confirmed user-facing outage. The most likely cause is a misconfigured or absent SWARM_BASE_URL / LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable pointing to a non-existent or incompatible harness deployment for the production-api runtime.
